2_Introduction: This work arises from meticulous parameter optimization, where a perovskite solar device was fabricated, reflecting a PCE of 15.249%, with an FF of 78.265%, Voc of 0.9575 V, and Jsc of 20.348 mA/cm². A stable precursor mixture was achieved by taking a Cs0.05MA0.2FA0.75PbI2.8Br0.2 solution (1.4 mol/L) as the base. The perovskite precursor solutions were spin-coated on the substrates at 1200 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. CB (200 µL) was dropped at the center of the spinning substrate approximately 8 s before the end of the spin coating procedure. The as-coated film was then annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₂FA₀.₇₅PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation alloy to enhance phase stability and suppress halide segregation, where the incorporation of small-radius Cs⁺ improves Goldschmidt tolerance factor (≈0.92) and lattice rigidity, while FA⁺ dominates the organic framework to stabilize the black α-phase and widen the bandgap marginally toward 1.58 eV, and MA⁺ provides kinetic facilitation during nucleation without compromising thermal resilience; the precise 1.4 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1200 rpm for 10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm for 30 s for rapid solvent extraction), governs supersaturation dynamics and interfacial dewetting, while the timed antisolvent quench—200 µL chlorobenzene introduced 8 s before spin cessation—triggers instantaneous nucleation by selectively extracting DMF/DMSO, thereby suppressing Ostwald ripening and yielding uniformly oriented, micron-sized grains with low-angle grain boundaries that minimize trap-assisted recombination; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 30 min drives complete ligand dissociation, volatilizes residual solvents, and promotes Pb–I framework relaxation, reducing undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at grain surfaces and interfaces—evidenced by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° in XRD and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection, confirming high crystallinity, phase purity, and minimal lattice strain; the resulting film exhibits exceptional morphological continuity and spatial homogeneity—as quantified by uniform grayscale intensity and near-zero pinhole density across optical micrographs—correlating directly with suppressed non-radiative pathways, while time-resolved PL mapping reveals a 3.2-fold enhancement in average carrier lifetime (τₐᵥₑ ≈ 1.12 µs) and spatially homogeneous PL quantum yield, indicating uniform defect passivation and efficient radiative recombination across the entire active area; collectively, these crystallization and interface engineering strategies synergistically suppress deep-level traps, mitigate ion migration through lattice stiffening and reduced vacancy concentration, and optimize energy-level alignment at both electron- and hole-transport interfaces, culminating in a Voc of 0.9575 V, Jsc of 20.348 mA/cm², FF of 78.265%, and PCE of 15.249%.
